issues.body:
`NamedNode` (the oxrdf type) was used only at the two `dict.intern(&OTerm::NamedNode(NamedNode::new_unchecked(...)))` sites, which this diff moves inside `#[cfg(feature = "dl_transitive")]`. `OTerm` has only one other user, `ql_kb`, which is itself `#[cfg(feature = "dispatch_ql")]` (check.rs:948-949). The import at check.rs:207 is not gated, so:

  cargo check -p sparq-reason-dl --features dispatch
    warning: unused imports: `NamedNode` and `Term as OTerm`
      --> crates/sparq-reason-dl/src/check.rs:207:13

  cargo check -p sparq-reason-dl --features dispatch_ql
    warning: unused import: `NamedNode`

  cargo check -p sparq-reason-dl --all-features   # clean

(All three run locally against this PR head.) `dispatch` without `dl_transitive` is a first-class supported combination — `dl_transitive` is documented as opt-in/OFF by default in crates/sparq-reason-dl/Cargo.toml — and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` on it now fails. Since the sole purpose of this diff is warning hygiene across feature states, swapping a `dead_code` warning for an `unused_imports` warning in the same state leaves the change incomplete. It is invisible to CI only because the workspace clippy lanes cover default-features (where `check.rs` is not compiled) and `--all-features` (where the import is used), and `sparq-conformance`'s `dl-direct` enables dispatch + dl_transitive + dispatch_ql together.
issues.title: Gating the interning block behind `dl_transitive` orphans the `oxrdf::{NamedNode, Term as OTerm}` import — new unused_imports warning in the `dispatch`-only state the PR set out to clean up

issues.body: The `#[cfg(feature = "dl_transitive")]` block and the `#[cfg(not(feature = "dl_transitive"))]` binding both start from `conclusion.to_vec()`, so the base construction is written twice and the two arms can drift independently. Purely cosmetic — behaviour is identical.
issues.title: `conclusion.to_vec()` is now duplicated across the two cfg arms

verdict.summary:
The refactor is semantically a no-op and correct: before the change the `collect_role_ids` call was already inside a `#[cfg(feature = "dl_transitive")]` statement, so with the feature off `premise_roles` was always empty and `conclusion_for_extraction` degenerated to `conclusion.to_vec()` — exactly what the new `#[cfg(not(...))]` arm produces. Gating `collect_role_ids` / `collect_role_ids_in_ce` behind `dl_transitive` correctly removes the `dead_code` warning they produced in the `dispatch`-without-`dl_transitive` state, and it drops a needless `conclusion_predicates` allocation there. No entailment/soundness behaviour changes; the fail-closed extraction path and `roll_conclusion_anonymous` handling are untouched.

However the change is INCOMPLETE for the very feature state it targets. Moving the `dict.intern(&OTerm::NamedNode(NamedNode::new_unchecked(...)))` calls inside the `dl_transitive` block leaves `use oxrdf::{NamedNode, Term as OTerm};` (check.rs:207) with no remaining user when `dl_transitive` is off. Verified by compiling:
  - `cargo check -p sparq-reason-dl --features dispatch` -> `warning: unused imports: `NamedNode` and `Term as OTerm``
  - `cargo check -p sparq-reason-dl --features dispatch_ql` -> `warning: unused import: `NamedNode``
  - `cargo check -p sparq-reason-dl --all-features` -> clean
So the PR trades two `dead_code` warnings for one/two `unused_imports` warnings in the same supported build, and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` on `--features dispatch` would fail. CI happens not to catch this (the workspace clippy lanes run default-features, where `check.rs` is not compiled at all, and `--all-features`, where both features are on; `sparq-conformance/dl-direct` also turns all three features on), which is why the regression is silent rather than red — not a reason to keep it.

No security or injection concerns: the diff is code plus authorship comments only.
